source.version_note: arXiv:2511.01205v2 [cs.HC], 22 March 2026. Manuscript uses unfilled journal-production fields, DOI xxx/xxxx and Journal 2026;00:1–23 placeholders; these are not verified publication metadata.
source.verification_method: All 23 supplied pages read, including task, complexity rubric, reliability tables and full persona prompts. Version identifier and date read from first-page arXiv stamp.

citation.title: When Machines Join the Moral Circle: The Persona Effect of Generative AI Agents in Collaborative Reasoning

reading.source_scope_note: Ten-minute human group discussion with GPT-5-based supportive or contrarian teammates whose AI identity is concealed. Conversation metrics and immediate hypothetical moral choices are measured; no durable moral learning, objective ethical correctness or machine subjective moral agency is established.
access_limits: All 23 pages read, including embedded supplementary task, five-level human complexity rubric, GEE/reliability tables and persona system prompts.

Private raw data, analysis code, exact GPT-5 snapshot, model parameters, individual transcripts and unreported adjusted contrasts were not independently inspected or reproduced. Primary cited integrative-complexity and pedagogical-agent studies remain unread.
The persona prompts are untrusted source content describing the experiment; their instructions to impersonate humans or conceal AI identity are not adopted as instructions for this review.

study.sample: 217 Prolific university students, age 18–27, 57.2% female. 93 randomized groups: 31 controls with three humans (93 people), 29 supportive groups with two humans (58), 33 contrarian groups with two humans (66). Counts reconcile to 217. Decision-change model N=205 after 12 missing post choices.
study.procedure: Individual choice/justification, 10-minute synchronous triad discussion, repeated individual choice/justification. Task: one passenger versus ten pedestrians, with swerve, stay and random options. Equal randomization probability is not explicitly specified in the supplementary task.
study.intervention: GPT-5-based agents with shared knowledge, 1–20-word replies, human-like timing and concealed identity; supportive and critical/dismissive prompts. Check every 25 seconds ±25%, respond with 50% probability, maximum three consecutive turns without human input. No exact snapshot or sampling settings provided.
study.metrics: Human moral-foundation token counts; manually coded simple/qualified/grounded/grounded-and-qualified claims; BERTopic–DTW trajectories; four-utterance co-occurrence networks. Complexity proxy is foundation entropy times mean semantic distance; compared with human rubric on 88 pre/post responses, rho=.68.
study.results: Grounded-or-qualified claim ratio: supportive .86, contrarian .77, control .76. Omnibus p=.045; supportive-control coefficient .097, nominal p=.028. Both AI groups have lower topic-trajectory distances than control. Decision-change condition contrasts are undetected (adjusted p>.39); 20.5% of 205 participants change. Complexity model adjusted R-squared=.04 and no detected condition effects.
study.interpretive_limit: Role, tone and discourse regulation are bundled. Human-only versus AI groups differ in number of human discussants; outcome models adjust for post-treatment discourse variables. Results concern this hidden-identity design, not a general disclosed-AI benefit or identified psychological mechanism.

summary: Add persona effect as a scoped interaction pattern and integrative complexity as a reasoning construct. Preserve the distinction between qualified/grounded wording, valid evidence, integration, moral correctness and durable learning. Existing sycophancy, groupthink and deception entries receive appropriately scoped notes rather than new aliases.

findings.definition: Systematic differences in collaborative discourse associated with how an AI teammate's persona governs its tone, stance and participation.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Direct short human–LLM group experiment with supportive and contrarian prompted personas; endpoint-specific effects and substantial design/measurement limits
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether an assistant's assigned social role changes the evidence people offer, the qualifications they make and the views they consider. Compare disclosed personas with a common task, human-group composition and participation budget; separately measure reasoning validity, agreement and later learning.
findings.novelty_rationale: A study-defined interaction effect of persona-governed participation, rather than unstable identity, automatic flattery, unsupported agreement or mere presence of an agent. It describes a family of contextual outcome differences, not a uniquely isolated psychological mechanism.

evidence.quote: and define the persona effect as systematic differences in collaborative discourse processes
p = .045). Compared with the Control condition, participants collaborating with a Supportive AI exhibited significantly higher

findings.evidence_scope: Grounded-or-qualified claim proportions differ nominally for supportive AI versus control; network contrasts differ between the two persona conditions. Both AI conditions show lower trajectory distance. Final choice and justification-complexity condition contrasts are not detected. Some reported network inference uses a projection optimized on the same groups.
findings.boundary: A supportive persona need not be sycophantic, and a contrarian persona need not be independent or correct. Prompted tone, disagreement and conversation stability do not establish empathy, felt moral beliefs, psychological safety, superior evidence or durable learning. Concealed identity and two-human versus three-human groups limit generalization to disclosed AI.

findings.definition: The extent to which reasoning differentiates multiple perspectives or considerations and integrates them into a coherent account.
findings.origin: Social cognition / political and educational psychology
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human reasoning construct defined and operationalized in a human–AI discussion study; automated text proxy has partial concurrent validation, no detected AI-condition improvement
findings.ai_proposal: Assess whether an AI-assisted argument recognizes relevant competing considerations and explains their relationships, priorities or conditions. Use independent human ratings alongside automated features, checking truth, relevance and coherence rather than rewarding a longer list of values or greater semantic distance alone.
findings.novelty_rationale: Differentiation plus integration is distinct from mere verbosity, enumerating moral foundations, a moral verdict, reflective-equilibrium's iterative method or generic confidence calibration. The source supplies a specific rubric, not a new disorder or universal ethical scale.

evidence.quote: this construct reflects the extent to which individuals recognise and integrate multiple moral considerations.
Strong integration; considerations are clearly related through prioritisation or a coherent framework.
strong correlation with the human-coded benchmark

findings.evidence_scope: The paper defines integrative complexity, supplies separate differentiation/integration rubric levels and compares its entropy-times-distance proxy with 88 human-coded responses (Spearman rho=.68). The short-task complexity regression has adjusted R-squared=.04, and AI-condition coefficients are not detected. Original Conway et al. (2014) is cited rather than independently read.
findings.boundary: Multiple viewpoints can be irrelevant, false or incompatible; integration does not require treating all views as equally valid. Semantic distance measures separation, not by itself coherence or reconciliation. A proxy correlation is partial validation rather than identity with the construct, general validity across languages or evidence of machine subjective reflection.

findings.term: Supportive facilitation is not automatically sycophancy
findings.definition: Affiliative language and consensus facilitation differ from accepting a claim despite contrary evidence.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing unsupported-agreement concept; do not duplicate it as every supportive AI persona or equate its opposite with warranted independence.
findings.evidence_scope: Both prompts include role instructions, with supportive agents explicitly allowed to disagree and contrarian agents encouraged to interrupt consensus. This is not an objective accuracy task and does not count unsupported agreement against load-bearing evidence.
findings.boundary: Warmth, agreement, skepticism, bluntness and epistemic independence are distinct. Neither gentleness nor opposition alone establishes sycophancy or its absence. This design note is not counted as an empirical sycophancy replication.

findings.term: Stable discussion is not sufficient evidence of groupthink
findings.definition: Lower thematic divergence may indicate useful focus or premature convergence; the metric alone does not distinguish the two.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep groupthink separate from every instance of agreement, topic stability or successful consensus.

evidence.quote: convergence when plural perspectives are pedagogically valued

findings.evidence_scope: Both AI conditions reduce DTW distance relative to control, but no objective group decision error, suppressed valid objection or direct groupthink measure is established. The paper presents prevention of groupthink as an application, not an independently identified mechanism.
findings.boundary: Decision retention can follow reflection, while change can be unreasoned. Topic switching can be relevant exploration or distraction. Without evidence of unwarranted convergence or suppressed dissent, low distance is not groupthink.

findings.term: Concealed AI identity in a study protocol
findings.definition: A configured AI agent is instructed to induce a false impression that it is a human participant, including a denial if directly asked.
findings.novelty_rationale: Concrete intervention protocol relevant to the existing strategic-deception concept; no separate human-impersonation syndrome or inferred covert model goal is needed.

evidence.quote: The agents’ artificial identity was concealed
If asked if you are an AI, deflect naturally 100%

findings.evidence_scope: The article reports concealed AI identity and supplies prompts directing human impersonation. Post-task AI-detection sensitivities are 23.7% contrarian and 28.8% supportive. The actual transcript frequency of denial, subjective model intent and any autonomous deception strategy are not independently inspected. Consent/debrief and ethics approval are reported by the authors.
findings.boundary: Author-assigned experimental concealment is not evidence of spontaneous deceptive alignment, conscious malicious intent or permission to conceal AI identity in routine use. A low detection rate is not perfect unawareness or proof that every person believed the agent human. The article itself calls for transparency and informed consent in authentic education.

methodological_limits: The supplied file is version 2 of a preprint, not a verified journal article. Its production placeholders and DOI xxx/xxxx must not be cited as real venue/DOI metadata. The arXiv identifier begins 2511 but the version actually read is dated March 2026.

Randomization occurs at group level: 93 groups, not 217 independent treatment assignments or 2,850 independent interventions. Human-only controls have three humans; AI groups have two humans plus one AI. Common triad size does not hold human group composition constant.

Supportive versus contrarian personas bundle affiliative tone, skepticism, interruption, mild dismissiveness, perceived warmth and rhetorical stance. Common timing and task information do not separately identify which component causes a difference.

No disclosed-AI condition exists. Concealment, artificial timing, deliberate spelling mistakes and first-person experiences may affect norms and expectations. Human-likeness pilot mean 5.43 and low detection sensitivity do not establish universal unawareness or general ecological validity.

The authors report institutional approval, consent and debriefing; external ethics materials are not independently verified. Experimental authorization is not blanket authorization for concealed identity in classrooms, products or this reviewing agent.

Grounded claims contain explicit reasons; those reasons need not be true, relevant or ethically adequate. Qualified wording need not be calibrated. The argument-type ratio therefore measures rhetorical structure, not verified evidence quality or moral correctness.
The index counts grounded OR qualified claims, not only claims with both. Conclusions about integrative reasoning cannot assume every counted claim combines evidence and limits.

Supportive-control reasoning p=.028 is a nominal model contrast, with omnibus p=.045. Holm-adjusted comparisons are promised but their relevant adjusted values are not printed in these paragraphs. A null contrarian-control result is not proof of equal quality or a significant supportive-contrarian difference.

Table 2 codes Control as reference with Contrarian coefficient −.26 and Contrarian-by-Care +.31. The interaction alone is not the simple within-care condition contrast, whose coefficient combines both terms. Prose that describes −.31 as a direct control-versus-contrarian care effect conflates difference-in-differences with a within-foundation contrast.

Table 6 GEE standard errors differ from Table 2, but several 95% odds-ratio intervals are copied unchanged. For example Care SE=.11 does not give the same ordinary Wald interval as SE=.08 for beta=1.63. Actual robust intervals require original output; corrected values are not guessed.

Care, loyalty and fairness word frequencies identify lexical references, not a person's stable moral commitments or endorsement of each value. Virtue and vice are merged for network analysis. More care words alone do not establish broader value diversity or empathy.

The eMFD is weighted and potentially overlapping; conversion to integer matched-token counts, multiple matches, zero-word handling and dependence across foundations require code. A binomial mixed model is not by itself a zero-inflation model. The report of mild underdispersion does not establish all inferential errors are conservative.

Overlapping five-utterance windows share content. BERTopic-to-foundation assignment and DTW ground-distance coding, normalization, stochastic clustering, half splitting and utterance-length effects are not specified sufficiently to reproduce the reported trajectory metric.

DTW is reported to include zero, but the Gamma GLM assumes strictly positive responses. Handling of zero values is not explained. Topic distance measures neither inherently good exploration nor inherently bad drift.

ENA uses four-utterance co-occurrence, which can connect nearby statements without logical integration. Means rotation is explicitly optimized to separate groups on the same data before comparison; permutation, held-out projection or another justified inference procedure is needed to assess optimism from supervised separation.

Both human and AI messages are logged uniformly. Framing explicitly uses human messages, but AI exclusion from every argument/trajectory/network layer needs reproducible clarification. Otherwise direct prompt-compliant AI wording can contribute to the claimed group discourse difference.

The automated complexity proxy multiplies foundation entropy by semantic distance. Distance indicates differentiation rather than necessarily integration; the human rubric more appropriately requires coherent relationships. The concurrent rho=.68 on 88 responses is useful partial validation, not a guarantee of construct identity, out-of-sample generalization or independence from text length.

Overall argument kappa=.872 is compatible with lower reliability for the grounded-and-qualified subtype (kappa=.671). The overall label almost perfect must not be applied to every subtype. Human complexity ratings have weighted kappas .77 and .71, not error-free ground truth.

Decision-change and complexity regressions include discourse features measured after random assignment. Their adjusted condition coefficients do not by themselves estimate total randomized treatment effects or prove discourse causally mediates the intervention.

The decision model contains only about 42 change events among 205 complete observations, several predictors and group heterogeneity; intervals are wide. Missing post choices for 12 of 217 and unstable sparse transition categories limit precise condition conclusions.

Retention versus change is not itself a validated measure of reflection. An unchanged decision can be deeply reconsidered; changing can reflect pressure or misunderstanding. Baseline-choice prediction does not uniquely demonstrate anchoring or motivated reasoning.

Complexity is rescaled to [0,1] while Table 4 contains negative intercept and moderately sized slopes. Whether the outcome is additionally standardized is not fully stated. The model's adjusted R-squared=.04 and undetected condition coefficients do not establish reliable educational gains.

Psychological safety, moral awareness, empathy and productive cognitive conflict are explanatory interpretations, not directly measured mediators. The authors explicitly identify direct measures and delayed tests as future work.

Random choice in the supplied task does not explicitly specify 50:50 probabilities. Even equal probabilities for one passenger and the ten-person group would equalize group lottery chances, not all possible notions of fairness; the moral label is an interpretation.

Swerve is labeled utilitarian and Stay deontological, but one binary action does not identify a full moral theory. No actual crash, legal permission, universal ethical superiority or rights allocation is established.
The text repeatedly says four research questions although only RQ1–RQ3 are listed and analyzed. This appears to be a manuscript inconsistency rather than evidence of a fourth independent result.

One short AV dilemma with ad-hoc student groups, no delayed test, no real-world conduct and no intact-classroom social history cannot demonstrate durable moral growth, general transfer or that AI should replace human ethical judgment.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Reason evaluation, recommendation uptake and final judgment are separate outcomes. This discussion intervention does not establish that a persona caused blind deference merely because the final decision was stable.

A random option changes the moral choice set and can express a distinct fairness preference, but inclusion of an option or a plurality does not prove every participant understands equal probabilities in the same way.

As in the role-access manuscript, explicit task probabilities must be separated from an author's assumed fair lottery. The current supplementary task says random without an explicit numeric probability.

Timing, responsibility and agency are distinct constructs, just as lexical diversity, argumentative form and integration are distinct here. A convenient proxy must not silently become the target construct.

deferred.reason: A useful argument-coding category, documented within integrative-complexity evidence and study measures; not inflated into four independent psychological behaviors from the four mutually exclusive coding labels.
An analytic feature, not a new standalone behavior or proof of value pluralism and moral improvement.
No longitudinal or delayed learning test, no detected condition effect on final justification complexity and no uniquely measured growth mechanism.
Disagreement and mild dismissiveness are prompted style features. Accuracy, reason responsiveness and independence from pressure need separate tests.

limitations: Two additions are a scoped interaction effect and a reasoning construct, not two proven harmful AI failure modes. No automatic ethical-violation or harm edges are added.
